name: Autodesk AutoCAD (2016-2025)
summary: Does NOT work through Wine: the installer, the licensing/sign-in service and the DirectX 11 canvas all fail.
notes:
AutoCAD does not run through Wine or Proton on Lindos or any other Linux. The modern installer (Autodesk Access / ODIS) needs .NET 4.8 + WPF with a working WebView2 sign-in, the licence manager (AdskLicensingService) has to run as a Windows service that talks to Autodesk's servers, and the drawing canvas uses DirectX 11 with features Wine's DXVK path does not cover for CAD (2D hardware acceleration falls back to a very slow software mode or crashes). Old releases (2007-2010) can be coaxed into starting but cannot activate. Autodesk does not support Linux and blocks it explicitly.
What you can use on Lindos:
- AutoCAD Web (web.autocad.com) - part of every AutoCAD subscription; opens/edits DWG in the browser (Edge/Chrome recommended).
- FreeCAD - free parametric 3D CAD with a 2D drafting workbench, imports/exports DWG via the ODA converter and DXF natively.
- LibreCAD / QCAD - free 2D CAD, DXF native, DWG import (QCAD Pro).
- BricsCAD (commercial) and Bricsys' DWG-native tools ship a real Linux build; so does ODA's free DWG viewer.
- Fusion 360 (Autodesk) has no Linux build either; Onshape (web) is a full parametric alternative.

alternatives.name: AutoCAD Web
alternatives.how: https://web.autocad.com - included with an AutoCAD subscription, works in Edge/Chrome/Firefox
